the connectivity probability of 2-D or 3-D mesh multicomputer networks can be arbitrarily close to 0 when the network size becomes large.
2-D and three-dimensional mesh networks are highly reliable in the view of realistic fault model.
2-D and especially 3-D mesh interconnection networks are very fault-tolerant in realistic situations.

the fault-tolerant performance of mesh network under a more realistic failure model.
the probabilistic analysis of mesh networks.
the fundamental question of how many faulty nodes a large mesh network can tolerate.

2-D and/or 3-D mesh multicomputer systems are highly reliable and can tolerate a large fraction of faulty nodes.
the 2-D and the 3-D mesh topologies are very reliable for multicomputer applications.
2-D and especially 3-D mesh multicomputer systems are reliable enough for practical use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mesh networks are among the best interconnection network topologes in terms of fault tolerance.
the 2-D and the 3-D mesh are the most reliable interconnection network toplogies for large multicomputers.
the 2-D and the 3-D mesh topologies can tolerate a large amount of faults, and the fault-tolerance capability is not significantly affected by the network size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mesh networks can be highly fault tolerant when the node failure probability in each network node is very small.
worst-case analysis is not always a good guide for practical design and evaluation.
the fault tolerance of mesh networks can be much better than what is suggested by worst-case analysis.
